fx.basis: interbank observed 5 August 2026; original currency governs

conventions.fx: EUR 1 = GBP 0.8575, interbank observed 5 August 2026; carried from the deal's European ceiling-cohort research pack and the investment memorandum. Original currency governs throughout.
conventions.rates_uk: Business rates estimated as the 2026 rating list rateable value (VOA, retrieved 8-27 July 2026) multiplied by 0.555, the England standard non-domestic rating multiplier for 2025/26. The 2026/27 multipliers are not verified in this work and all four UK properties sit in the rateable-value band of GBP 500,000 and above, where a higher multiplier applies from April 2026 - so this figure is more likely to understate than overstate the charge. Understating rates understates GOP, because GOP sits above the rates line and EBITDA is the calibration target.
conventions.insurance: Property insurance set at 1.0% of total revenue where no figure is filed; a stated convention, not an observation.
conventions.ffe: FF&E reserve set at 3.0% of total revenue in every book. No filed account carries this line, so NOI is a modelled measure throughout and is not comparable to any published profit figure.
conventions.franchise: Brand franchise fee set to zero in every book. None of the ten pays a franchise royalty on the evidence held, and operator base and incentive fees are excluded from all ten - the same convention the Fawley model uses, where the P&L NOI line sits before the operator incentive and the asset-management fee.
conventions.ground_rent: Ground rent set to zero in every book. Where a lease rental is disclosed (Cliveden GBP 420k, Estelle Manor GBP 655k, Beaverbrook GBP 294k of other operating lease rentals) it already sits inside the filed operating profit and therefore inside the calibrated EBITDA; carrying it again below EBITDA would double-count it.
conventions.wages_fixed: All direct wages are modelled as variable. No fixed wage base is carried, which is the right shape for a seasonal operator and mildly flattering for a year-round one in a trough quarter.
conventions.und_fixed: A year-round administrative and general fixed base of 6,000 per key is carried in every book so that a seasonal property still bears overhead in its closed quarters. The cost scalar multiplies it.
conventions.payroll_bridge: The template does not split undistributed costs into wages and expenses, so a filed all-staff payroll figure cannot be read straight off the engine. The bridge used throughout is: implied all-staff payroll = total direct wages + 0.65 x administrative and general + 0.45 x sales and marketing + 0.40 x property operations and maintenance. The three shares are a stated convention.
conventions.cost_per_employee: Where payroll is derived from a headcount, the cost per average employee is anchored on three filed measurements: Cliveden GBP 34,802, Estelle Manor GBP 35,529, Beaverbrook GBP 28,453 (each staff cost divided by average monthly employees, same filing). GBP/EUR 33,000-40,000 is used, stated per hotel.
conventions.seasonality_convention: Quarterly demand indices are normalised so that their available-day-weighted mean over the quarters the hotel is OPEN equals 1.00. For seasonal properties the four-quarter sum is therefore below 4.00, which departs from the template's own convention; the departure is deliberate, because an index summing to 4 over two open quarters would earn a full year of spa and ancillary revenue in half a year. Occupancy for a seasonal property is therefore on an open-days (net) basis, not a calendar basis.
conventions.achieved_rate: Lead-in rates are the cheapest publicly bookable room. Achieved ADR is higher because of room mix. An achieved-rate factor of 1.15 is applied where the lead-in is a genuine cheapest-room rate across a wide mix, 1.10 for small all-suite properties, and 1.00 for Le Grand Controle, whose 14-suite calendar median already spans the whole inventory. The factor is a stated convention, not a measurement, and it is the single largest judgement in the rooms line.
conventions.money_basis: CALIBRATED books sit in the money of their filing year (FY2024 or FY2025). ESTIMATED books sit in 2026 money at rates observed in July and August 2026. No inflation bridge is applied between the two, and inflation inside each ten-year model is set to zero so every year is identical. Margins are ratios and are unaffected by the money basis; revenue per key is not.

subject.name: Fawley Court
subject.basis: Year 7 stabilised, year-7 money (Align model, Financial Model v29 at the ruled GBP 50m entry)
subject.note: Taken from the deal's own measurement record for v29 (Model/docs/v29-figures.json), measured on a scratch copy of the saved workbook on 19 August 2026. The record publishes total revenue, GOP and NOI and a split of revenue by department, so the revenue rows are filled here for the first time: rooms GBP 16,492,406; food and beverage GBP 21,410,754 as one line, because the record does not split food from beverage; spa GBP 5,746,795; memberships GBP 2,478,845; room hire GBP 603,186; and a balance of GBP 405,800 sitting on the P&L's remaining revenue lines, which the record does not name individually. The six sum to total revenue. On the row structure this pack uses, the ten comparables carry conferencing and events room hire inside the food line, so the subject's room hire belongs with food and beverage when the columns are read across. The departmental cost rows stay blank: the record publishes no cost of sales, departmental expense, direct wage or undistributed line for the subject, and a departmental profit cannot be built without them. Year 7 is in year-7 money: the ADR chain runs GBP 1,000 in year 1 to GBP 1,160 in year 7, so revenue per key is not on the same money basis as the ten comparables. Margins are ratios and are unaffected by the money basis. NOTE the NOI basis: the operator's base and incentive fees are charged inside the P&L, so this NOI is after them, while every comparable in this pack carries no operator fee at all. Only the GOP line is like-for-like.
